title: Code-fact scanner (AST): mechanically list every write/read/external call/entry point to ground planning and implementation
body: Port SmartMemory's scanner. A static AST pass (Python ast; TS via the compiler API or ts-morph) enumerates every side-effect atom: store, op, file:line, enclosing function. Call-graph propagation finds the entry points that reach each atom, with edges marked exact vs name_only. A runtime pass instruments the real drivers under the existing tests, and a merge unions the two. LLMs (explorers, planners, reviewers) then annotate a given list instead of discovering it, so 'did the plan cover every write path' becomes a set check. SM measured precision 0.90 against runtime and byte-identical reruns; the scanner was Codex-authored and the merge run cost $0.57 / 16 min. Gotchas: exclude import-time reads; ContextVar .set and read-shaped queries false-positive as writes. Source: smart-memory-docs/docs/features/FULL-ALIGN-1/facts/sink_inventory.py + merge_atoms.py, phase0-ledger.md. Forge prior art (checked 2026-10-05): no AST tooling in compose/stratum; design exploration is LLM-only (compose-explorer, COMP-EXPLORER-EVIDENCE-1); ANATOMY.md is hand-written and stale (says build.js 1536 lines, actual 8147); COMP-CANON-INVENTORY (PLANNED) needs exactly this list for canon write paths and is the natural first consumer.
source: SmartMemory 2.0 FULL-ALIGN-1 Phase 0 boundary-atom scanner, via smartmemory-5a (2026-10-05)

discussion.text: Owner 2026-10-05: forge uses SmartMemory, so build this ON SmartMemory instead of porting a standalone scanner. SM already ships the base layer: smartmemory/code/{parser,ts_parser,indexer}.py, exposed as MCP code_index / code_search / code_dependencies / code_dead_code (smart-memory-mcp/.../tools/code_tools.py). compose/.mcp.json registers smartmemory-memory. The FULL-ALIGN-1 boundary scanner itself imports SM's CodeParser + SymbolTable (sink_inventory.py:37-39). Gap found 2026-10-05: zero code_* tool calls across all Claude Code transcripts (tools offered, never invoked), and no evidence forge has ever been indexed. So step 1 is to index forge with code_index and have compose explorers/planners call it. The forge-specific part is only the atom classifiers (which writes count as canon/state). Unverified: whether ts_parser covers forge's plain JS (compose is .js/.jsx).
